title: The fullness of the feast of the Ascension
english: Blessed be God. As a head is to the body, so a feast is to the order of feasts; and today is that feast. For we celebrate the Ascension of Christ in the flesh, as the fullness shown of the Lordly feasts. Just as a head is beautiful, so today's feast of divine grace radiates beauty; but many, not knowing its greatness, think it is less.

If you wish to learn, lend me your mind with forbearance. Cooperate with me only through prayers, I entreat you; and silence the leaden winds, and calm the waves of chatter, and grant me leisure for hearing. For according to wise Solomon, the words of the wise are heard in rest.

First, then, is the terrible and wonderful feast: the birth of Christ according to the flesh. For how is the descent of God from heaven to us not wonderful, but rather a co-descent? Because the Master of all condescended to unite himself to the form of a servant, and the one encompassing all has a poor mother.

Second is the feast of the Theophanies, having a much greater contemplation than the first. For in the first feast, a star showed the God-Logos having been born; but in the second feast, John cried, 'Behold the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world.' And the Father, crying from heaven, confirmed the testimony of the one being baptized: 'This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.' But even then, the full enjoyment of sobriety was not reached, since the mortal body had not yet received immortality through the resurrection.

Third is the feast of the saving passion: the resurrection, which gives life to those who, through his blood, are being struck like sparks, and are being reborn through water and the Holy Spirit. Therefore, he raised a fallen world, and enabled the formerly fallen Adam to reach eternal life. Through a tree Adam tasted death; through the tree of the cross, life is granted to the world. And this feast was shown more glorious than the preceding feasts, because in it, death, through death, having killed death, brought immortal life to those dying. But even this did not have the fullness of joy, holding the risen one upon the earth.

But the great and surpassing joy of Pentecost, in which the Holy Spirit was given to the apostles, is today, in the day of the Ascension, filled with joy through all things. Having opened the moon-bearing heavens, and having ascended the most fine air, and having rounded from the earth to the heavenly grips, and having incited all the natures of the angels to unutterable joy, he showed us a strange sight: our flesh having been placed upon a royal throne.
